title: A typo then the right PIN collapses the pairing card at once
body:
## Summary
LinkState kept a PIN refusal through a successful pairing, so a viewer who mistyped and then typed the right PIN saw "wrong PIN" over the picture for the rest of the refusal's 5 s.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkState.kt:51` (PenPaired) set the pen but left `refusal`; `view` checks the refusal before the pen (`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkState.kt:64` before `:66`), so for REFUSED_MS after a typo the card read Refused over a paired pen. The rule two lines up (`:54`, a refusal must not cover the person drawing) held for a refusal arriving during a pen and broke for one arriving just before it. Fixed: PenPaired clears the refusal.

## Flow
- viewer types a wrong PIN -> TV shows Refused('wrong PIN')
- viewer types the right PIN within 5 s -> PenPaired
- view(t) for t < refusedAt + 5 s -> Refused over the paired pen (before); Chip (after)

## Expected impact
Every viewer who mistypes the PIN once: the card collapses the moment they pair. Measured by LinkStateTest case 6b. Could break: nothing reads the refusal after a pairing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the TV stops showing a refusal over a pen that has paired
Before: refused at 10.0 s, paired at 11.0 s: view at 11.0/12.0/14.999 s Refused 3 of 3; pen gone at 11.5 s read at 14.6 s Refused
After: Chip 3 of 3; Lost
Method: gate - LinkStateTest case 6b red then green under :core:test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkState.kt:51 `is LinkEvent.PenPaired -> copy(current = event.clientId, goneAtMs = null)` (refusal kept)
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkState.kt:64 refusal checked before `if (current != null) return LinkView.Chip` (:66)
:core:test before: LinkStateTest > case 6b FAILED at LinkStateTest.kt:71

title: On the relay, a wrong PIN that unpairs the pen says why on the TV
body:
## Summary
A wrong hello on the shared (relay) conversation emitted the refusal before the unpairing, so the TV hid the refusal and showed a Wi-Fi blink, then 'Pen lost', with no reason.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt` sharedHello built `[refusal(WRONG_PIN), Unpaired]`. PenSessionHost carries effects out in order (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:53-89`): the refusal becomes PenRefused while the old pen still holds the link, and LinkState ignores a refusal during a pen (`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkState.kt:55-56`); the Unpaired then makes it PenGone. Two rules that must agree (effect order vs the reducer's gate). Fixed: Unpaired first, then the refusal. No wire change.

## Flow
- pen A paired through the relay
- a hello with a wrong PIN arrives on the same relay socket
- effects carried in order -> before: Chip for 3 s then Lost; after: Refused('wrong PIN') for 5 s then Lost

## Expected impact
The viewer whose pen dropped sees the reason instead of a network symptom. Could break: a consumer that relied on the refusal being first (only PenSessionHost consumes it; tv-app compile and unit tests green).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the TV names the cause when a wrong PIN unpairs the relay pen
Before: view at 2.0 s Chip, at 6.999 s Chip, at 7.0 s Lost
After: Refused, Refused, Lost
Method: gate - LinkStateTest case 6c replays PenSessionHost.carryOut on the conversation's effects; red then green. SharedPenConversationTest case 5 re-pinned to the new order
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/LinkState.kt:55-56 `is LinkEvent.PenRefused -> if (current != null) this else ...`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:53-62 Send -> PenRefused, :81-87 Unpaired -> PenGone, applied in list order
:core:test before: LinkStateTest > case 6c FAILED at LinkStateTest.kt:95

title: The pairing PIN is compared in constant time
body:
## Summary
PairingDesk.check compared the offered PIN with String ==, an early-exit compare; the registry's timing-defenses technique names every such equality on a secret path.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt` (PairingDesk.check) used `offered == pin`, which returns sooner the earlier the first wrong digit: a which-digit oracle to a LAN client timing round trips (software-engineering / device-pairing / timing-defenses: compare in constant time, audit every equality a secret value meets). `git grep` finds 1 equality on the PIN in core, tv-app and stick-app main sources. Fixed: `MessageDigest.isEqual` over UTF-8 bytes, whose time depends only on the offered length. The guess limit is unchanged (the lockout-as-DoS card is already filed and is not this).

## Flow
- LAN client sends hellos and times each refusal
- early-exit compare -> an offer with the right leading digits answers measurably later
- after: every same-length offer takes the same time

## Expected impact
Closes a timing channel on the pre-trust surface at no cost to the viewer. Could break: nothing; the same 5 PIN cases pair or refuse as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no early-exit equality on the pairing secret
Before: early-exit PIN equalities in core/src/main (comments stripped) 1
After: 0; right / one-off / prefix / longer / empty PIN pair or refuse identically (5 of 5)
Method: gate - PairingGuessLimitTest case 5 (source guard plus behaviour) red then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:73 (before) `if (offered == pin) {`
git grep -n 'pin\b.*==\|== *pin' -- core/src/main tv-app/src/main stick-app/src/main -> 1 hit
:core:test before: PairingGuessLimitTest > case 5 FAILED at PairingGuessLimitTest.kt:93

title: A seek, a hop or a step never lands past the clip's last frame
body:
## Summary
TransportPlan held seek- and a backward step at 0 but let seek+, seek and a forward step run past the end; it took durationMs and never read it.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/TransportPlan.kt` plan(): `seek-` and `step` coerced at 0; `seek+` (`positionMs + SEEK_HOP_MS`), `seek` and a forward `step` had no upper bound, and the `durationMs` parameter the shell passes (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:202`) had zero reads. Past the end was therefore the player's decision (REPEAT_MODE_ALL), though the plan's contract is that the shell decides nothing. A step value large enough to overflow `value.toLong() * FRAME_MS` wrapped to an arbitrary position. Fixed: every seek goes through inClip, [0, duration - one frame] when the duration is known, [0, unbounded) when it is 0.

## Flow
- remote Right at 18 s of a 20 s clip -> SeekTo(23000) before
- phone scrub at the far right -> seek value == duration -> SeekTo(20000) before
- after: SeekTo(19960), the last frame, in both

## Expected impact
A viewer hopping or stepping near the end stays on the clip's last frame instead of whatever Media3 does past the end. Could break: nothing inside the clip; unknown duration keeps today's behaviour. Not seen on a device.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - transport targets stay inside the clip
Before: 20 s clip: seek+ at 18 s 23000; seek 20000/25000 -> 20000/25000; step +1 on the last frame 20000; step 1e18 from 1 s 3106511852580897768 (wrapped); seek commands that can leave the clip 3 of 4 (seek+, seek, step; seek- was clamped)
After: 19960 in every case; 0 of 4; inside the clip and with unknown duration unchanged
Method: gate - ReviewModeTest case 6b red then green; case 6 GUARD unchanged
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/TransportPlan.kt:30-36 (before) `"seek+" -> listOf(PlayerAction.SeekTo(positionMs + SEEK_HOP_MS))`; `durationMs: Long = 0` read 0 times in plan
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:202 `durationMs = player.duration.coerceAtLeast(0)`
:core:test before: ReviewModeTest > case 6b FAILED at ReviewModeTest.kt:92
Correction: commit a06178fe's body gives the wrapped figure as 3_106_511_852_580_896_768 and '3 of 5 commands'; the figures here are the right ones.

title: A blank tag and pen input with no stroke open are counted as drops
body:
## Summary
Two drop paths in PenEngine left no trace in /health's dropped map: a tag whose label trims to nothing, and a move or up with no stroke open.

## Description
92297134 counted five drop paths; `core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt` handleTag returned silently on a blank label, and handlePen's `move` / `up` did nothing when `liveMeta` was null: the case where a down never arrived, or an undo or clear (the remote's Up or Down key) cut a stroke mid-gesture so the rest of the gesture vanishes, exactly the 'draws but nothing appears' question the map answers. Fixed: `tag-blank-label` and `pen-no-stroke`.

## Flow
- phone draws; the remote's Up (undo) lands mid-stroke -> clearLive
- the phone's remaining moves and its up arrive -> dropped
- /health dropped: {} before; {pen-no-stroke: n} after

## Expected impact
An operator reading /health can see why a stroke never appeared. Could break: a harness asserting an empty dropped map after stray moves (none found in tools/).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every decoded-and-dropped pen message is counted
Before: blank tag + stray move + stray up: dropped {}; silent drop paths 2
After: {pen-no-stroke: 2, tag-blank-label: 1}; 0; annotations 0 -> 0
Method: gate - DroppedMessagesTest new case red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:187 (before) `"move" -> if (liveMeta != null) livePoints += xyp`
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:231 (before) `if (label.isEmpty()) return`
:core:test before: DroppedMessagesTest > a blank tag and pen input with no stroke open are counted too() FAILED at :42

title: PenEngine's hold default is fixed at construction, not a public setter
body:
## Summary
PenEngine promises every public member holds its lock, but defaultHold was a public var whose setter took none; nothing writes it.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:34-36` (class KDoc): every public member holds this instance's lock, because the pen thread writes while the frame loop and heartbeat read. `core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:42` declared `var defaultHold`; its generated setter is unsynchronised while holdMs reads it under the lock. `git grep defaultHold` over core, tv-app, stick-app: 0 writers. Fixed: `val`.

## Flow
- any future caller sets engine.defaultHold from the UI thread
- the pen thread reads it in holdMs under the lock -> unsynchronised write (before)
- after: there is no setter

## Expected impact
Keeps the thread-safety promise true by construction. Could break: nothing; no writer exists.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the class's lock promise holds for every public member
Before: public setters on PenEngine 1 (setDefaultHold); writers 0
After: 0; writers 0
Method: gate - PenEngineThreadsTest reflection case red then green; tv-app compile green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:42 (before) `var defaultHold: Hold = Hold.Default,`
git grep -n defaultHold -- core tv-app stick-app -> the declaration and the holdMs read only
:core:test before: PenEngineThreadsTest > nothing public writes the engine from outside its lock() FAILED

title: The pairing card keeps a relay's session in the address it prints
body:
## Summary
PairingUrl.display dropped the whole query along with the PIN, so a relay address printed under the QR lost the `?session=` it needs to reach the TV.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PairingUrl.kt` display() ended `.substringBefore('?')`. The card prints it as the address to type when the QR will not scan (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:123`), and RelayTransport's phone side meets the TV at `/?session=abc` (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt:32`). Typed as printed, it reaches the relay and no TV. Fixed: only the PIN goes (the fragment, or an older `pin=` parameter).

## Flow
- relay phone URL http://relay/?session=a#pin=7
- card prints relay/ (before) -> typed by hand, no session
- after: card prints relay/?session=a

## Expected impact
A viewer typing the relay address by hand reaches their TV. LAN addresses print exactly as before. Could break: nothing prints the PIN (still 0 of 3).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the printed address reaches the TV
Before: relay addresses that keep their session 0 of 3; PIN printed 0 of 3
After: 3 of 3; 0 of 3; LAN 2 of 2 unchanged
Method: gate - PairingUrlTest new case red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PairingUrl.kt:14 (before) `...substringBefore('#').substringBefore('?')`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt:32 `the pen side meets it at /?session=abc`
:core:test before: PairingUrlTest > the card keeps the part of the address that reaches the TV ... FAILED at :29

title: Two KDocs no longer promise TV behaviour the TV does not have
body:
## Summary
AnnotationTimeline.progressAt claimed a TV fade-out and Smoothing.path claimed to be what the renderer uses; the TV does neither and both had zero callers.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Timeline.kt:12` 'used for fade-out on the TV': tv-app's Overlay draws `visibleAt` and nothing fades. `core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Smoothing.kt:83` 'what the renderer always wants': the renderer fits the spline itself, incrementally (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:214` StrokeRender). git grep: progressAt 0 callers, Smoothing.path 0 callers, tests included. Both removed; toCubics now says it is the reference the TV copies.

## Flow
- a reader trusts the KDoc and looks for the fade or the call site
- none exists (before)
- after: the docs name where the TV's spline really is

## Expected impact
Developers stop chasing a fade and a render path that do not exist. Could break: nothing called either (tv-app compile green).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - KDocs state only what the code does
Before: false TV claims 2; zero-consumer public functions 2
After: 0; 0
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep before, :core:test and :tv-app:compileDebugKotlin green after; no red-first test for a removal
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
git grep -n progressAt -> core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Timeline.kt:13 only
git grep -n 'Smoothing.path' -> none; `fun path(` at core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Smoothing.kt:84 only
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:48 `AnnotationTimeline(doc).visibleAt(tMs)` (no progressAt)

title: The TV draws a stroke's last span straight; the tested spline curves it
body:
## Summary
The spline the TV draws is a second implementation in tv-app's Overlay; core tests only Smoothing.toCubics, and the two already disagree on a committed stroke's last span.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Smoothing.kt:61-80` toCubics duplicates the last point and fits n-1 curved spans. `tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:279` fits a span only once kept[i+2] exists, so for a finished stroke the last span is never fitted and `drawPendingTail` (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:304-319`) draws it as a straight line, every frame, for as long as the stroke is on screen. The spline factor is copied by hand (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:195` SPLINE_K = 1/6 vs `tension / 6.0`). The JVM tests pin a curve the TV does not draw.

## Flow
- draw a curved stroke and lift
- core: last span a cubic
- TV: last span a straight segment from kept[n-2] to kept[n-1]

## Expected impact
The end of every stroke on the TV would match the tested curve, and a test would catch the next drift. Could break: Overlay draw cost (one more cubic per committed stroke).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the curve the TV draws is the one core tests
Before: curved spans for a committed n-point stroke: core n-1, TV n-2 (+1 straight); implementations of the span fit 2, tested 1
After: predicted: n-1 on both; 1 implementation (StrokeRender calls a core span function), tested
Method: simulation - read both fits over a 4-point stroke; the instrument needs tv-app (out of this round's paths)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/Smoothing.kt:70 `for (i in 1 until p.size - 2)` over first/last-duplicated points
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:279 `while (fittedSpans + 3 <= kept.size)`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:304 drawPendingTail draws the rest with drawLine
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:195 `SPLINE_K = 1.0 / 6.0`
instrument: Extract Smoothing.span(p0,p1,p2,p3,tension) in core, call it from StrokeRender.fitSpan, fit the final span on commit; a core test that a committed n-point stroke yields n-1 cubics equal to toCubics, red on A (n-2). Out-of-scope seam: tv-app/Overlay.kt.

title: Relay wrong PINs and lockouts leave no trace in the log or /health
body:
## Summary
On the relay (shared) conversation a wrong PIN or a lockout is a refusal with no Close, and only Close is logged; /health carries no pairing figures at all.

## Description
`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:53-62` sends a refusal and raises a LinkEvent with no log line; `tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:64-65` logs only on Close, which a shared conversation never emits (`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:208-210`). `core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/HealthBody.kt:13-30` HealthReading has no wrong-PIN or lockout count. So a guessing run against the relay, or a lockout that refused the owner, leaves nothing to read afterwards (device-pairing / timing-defenses: the ledger gets everything).

## Flow
- 5 wrong hellos through the relay -> lockout
- logcat: no line; /health: no field
- after: PairingDesk counts wrong PINs and lockouts; /health carries pairing:{wrong,lockouts}

## Expected impact
The operator can tell 'under guessing' from 'nobody tried'. Could break: /health consumers that parse strictly (tools read named fields only).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed pairing leaves a countable trace
Before: refusals on the relay that reach a log or /health: 0 of 6 (5 wrong + 1 locked, walked through PenSessionHost.carryOut)
After: predicted 6 of 6 in /health
Method: simulation - walked the effects through carryOut; the wiring is tv-app Health.kt / PenSessionHost (out of this round's paths)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PenSessionHost.kt:64-65 `is PenEffect.Close -> { Log.i(TAG, "pen rejected ...` (the only refusal log)
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt:208 `PinCheck.LOCKED -> return listOf(refusal(LOCKED, ...))` (no Close on shared)
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/HealthBody.kt:29 only `dropped` beyond the player and render fields
instrument: PairingDesk counters (wrongPins, lockouts) + HealthReading.pairing with a default, a HealthBodyTest and a shared-conversation test red on A (0 counted); wire in tv-app Health.kt. Out-of-scope seam: tv-app.

title: One undo press mid-stroke takes the stroke and the previous edit
body:
## Summary
An undo that arrives while a stroke is being drawn discards the live stroke and also undoes the last committed annotation: two things for one press.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:120-123` Undo runs `clearLive()` and then `history.undo(committed)`. The remote's Up key is undo (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:146`), so with one person drawing on the phone and another holding the remote, a single press removes the stroke in progress and the drawing before it; the phone's remaining moves and up are then dropped (now counted as pen-no-stroke). The registry's undo promise is one gesture back per press (undo-history golden path, gesture-coalescing).

## Flow
- phone: down, move... (stroke open)
- remote Up -> Undo
- before: live stroke gone AND last committed annotation gone; predicted after: only the live stroke goes (or the undo waits for the up)

## Expected impact
Two-person sessions stop losing a finished drawing to an undo aimed at the stroke in progress. Could break: what a viewer expects undo to do mid-stroke is a product choice, hence B.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one press undoes one thing
Before: annotations removed by one mid-stroke undo: 2 (live + last committed)
After: predicted 1
Method: simulation - traced accept(Undo) with a live stroke; a 10-line PenEngine test decides it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: PenEngine test: commit an arrow, open a stroke, accept(Undo) -> annotationCount; red on A (0, the arrow gone too), green when a live stroke absorbs the undo. Needs the owner's call on the intended semantics.

title: The eraser cannot grab a name tag by its label box
body:
## Summary
HitTest measures a name tag only at its anchor, but the TV and the phone draw the tag's label box well above the anchor, entirely outside the eraser's reach.

## Description
`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/HitTest.kt:51` 'Tags are small; treat the anchor as the target'. The TV draws the box from anchor - 0.063 h to anchor - 0.130 h (`tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:165-176`: textSize 0.042 h, lift 1.8 textSize), which on 16:9 is 0.035..0.073 content-width units above the anchor, while the default tolerance is 0.025 (`core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/HitTest.kt:15`). The phone's mirror draws its box 11-26 px above the anchor too (`companion/index.html:529-532`). So a viewer erasing a tag taps the label, the one thing they can see, and nothing happens.

## Flow
- draw a name tag
- pick Erase and tap its label box
- before: nothing erased (nearest box point 0.035 > 0.025); predicted after: the tag is erased

## Expected impact
Tags become erasable by what is drawn, like every other annotation. Could break: a tap on a stroke behind a tag's box now takes the tag (topmost wins, as for any overlap).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the eraser grabs a tag where it is drawn
Before: share of the drawn label box within tolerance of the anchor: 0% (nearest edge 0.035 vs 0.025)
After: predicted 100% (box region included in distanceTo)
Method: simulation - the box geometry computed from Overlay's constants; the fix needs those constants shared between core and tv-app (out of this round's paths)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/HitTest.kt:51 `is Annotation.NameTag -> metric.distance(x, y, a.anchor[0], a.anchor[1])`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:165-166 `textSize = rect.height * 0.042f`, `lift = textSize * 1.8f`; :175 `boxTop = anchorY - lift - textSize - padY`
(1.8-0.3)*0.042 = 0.063 h -> /1.778 = 0.035 content-width > DEFAULT_TOLERANCE 0.025 (HitTest.kt:15)
instrument: Move the tag layout constants (text size, lift, padding) into core, use them in HitTest.distanceTo and Overlay.drawNameTag; a HitTest case tapping the box centre red on A (picks nothing). Out-of-scope seam: tv-app/Overlay.kt.
